thread:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#KMS_PROXY_HIGH_429 — KMS proxy 5xx/429 rate spike for service=key-rotation (region: us-west-2). Initial failing rate 18% over 5m. Pager: @oncall-eng
PagerDuty: Incident assigned to Ajit K. — ack required
Ajit K.: acked. I'm taking it. pulling logs now. :eyes:
Maria H.: I'm on metrics. seeing a strong spike in `kms-proxy.requests` and `kms-rotation.worker_queue_length` around 22:41 UTC
Ben S.: logs from one of the proxies look like a retry loop flooding upstream, lots of `429` with backoff that then resets. snippet:
```
2026-03-14T22:41:12Z kms-proxy[pid=42]: POST /decrypt 429 service_quota
2026-03-14T22:41:12Z kms-rotator[worker=7]: rotate_key(key_id=ak-xyz) failed: rate_limit_exceeded
2026-03-14T22:41:13Z kms-rotator[worker=7]: scheduling retry in 0s (backoff state reset)
```
Ben S.: that "retry in 0s" is suspicious — looks like exponential backoff state was lost when a rotation job re-queued itself. we're getting feedback loop: many workers requeue immediately -> proxy overloaded -> 429s -> repeat
Ajit K.: Confirmed. topology: rotation workers write to shared queue; after a backend error they should backoff, but a change last week introduced a fast-requeue path for job state migration.
Maria H.: Key point: this is not a pure KMS outage. It's self-inflicted queue starvation due to rotation requeueing. customer impact: decrypts for newly rotated keys failing intermittently, some client requests see transient 429s and fall back to retries -> higher latency and some user-visible errors in 2% of requests for affected tenants.
SRE Lead: tagging severity P1 for on-call; need mitigation plan now. Two concurrent ideas: 1) stop rotation job globally, 2) apply smoothing/rate-limit at kms-proxy to shed and avoid cascading 429s. Which first?
Ajit K.: stop rotation job briefly — lower blast radius. I'll issue a quick job disable flag. Ben, can you patch the rotation worker to honor backoff before requeue? That needs a restart, so do the disable now and patch tomorrow.
Ben S.: on it. disabling the migratory requeue path now.
Ben S.: command I'm running:
```
kubectl -n platform set env deploy/kms-rotator DISABLE_FAST_REQUEUE=true
```
Ben S.: applied, scaling rotator down from 10 -> 0 to drain in-flight
IncidentBot: Deploy event: set env DISABLE_FAST_REQUEUE=true on deploy/kms-rotator by Ben S.
PagerDuty: Note — escalation to SRE Lead if not acknowledged in 10m
Maria H.: while rotation is paused, I recommend enabling an emergency fallback: allow kms-proxy to serve decrypted results from the cached-keys layer for up to 2 minutes. That will reduce user-visible failures while we stabilize.
Ajit K.: agree. Maria, can you flip cache TTL and add circuit-breaker config? We need to avoid cache thrash.
Maria H.: flipping cache mode to "read-through-fallback" now. command:
```
POST /admin/config/kms-proxy/cache
{"fallback_mode":"read-through-fallback","max_stale_sec":120}
```
Maria H.: cache fallback enabled. monitoring requests after change...
Ben S.: also rolled a temporary rate-limit smoothing patch on the proxy:
```
kubectl -n platform rollout restart deploy/kms-proxy
# new env: PROXY_RATE_SMOOTH_MS=500
```
Ben S.: restart completed, proxies are now returning 503 for sustained overload instead of immediate 429 spam; this should stop PD noise
Ajit K.: Observability check: `kms-proxy.429.rate` dropping from 18% -> 2% in last 3m. request latency normalizing. nice.
SRE Lead: Good. escalate to ops for customer communication: which tenants impacted and are we seeing any paid customer errors? Maria, can you assemble a short impact list.
Maria H.: pulling tenant error logs and will DM support. current estimate: 14 tenants had >1% error increase; 3 tenants (acct-abc, acct-xyz, acct-legacy) saw >5% error rate during window. no full-service outages, mostly elevated latency and retries. I'll draft a short blurb for status.redwood.ai
Lucy P.: I'll take the midnight handoff if this stays stable. @Ajit please include runbook pointer and any sticky steps.
Ajit K.: runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kms-rotation
Ajit K.: post-mitigation next steps: (1) revert cache fallback after rotation resumes, (2) patch rotation worker to persist backoff state, (3) add PD suppression rule for repeated identical signature in 5m, (4) write a test that simulates queue requeue storm.
Ben S.: opened PR for backoff fix: https://github.com/redwood/kms/pull/342 — includes unit tests and e2e gate. dropping into code review.
SRE Lead: timeline: pause rotation at 22:43, cache fallback enabled 22:46, proxy smoothing rolled 22:48. Current status: degraded (reduced error rate). assign follow-up actions and post-incident review tomorrow 1500 UTC.
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Ajit K.; escalated to SRE Lead. Current status: acknowledged.
Ajit K.: handing to Lucy for overnight watch. leaving notes in the runbook and will be available on pager if it flares.
Lucy P.: ack — will monitor `kms-proxy` and `rotation.worker_queue_length` dashboards. If 429s > 5% for 10m I will escalate to SRE Lead immediately.
SRE Lead: thanks team. please add any postmortem items to the incident board: #KMS-ROT-INC-1876543210
Maria H.: drafting status update and will post to #customer-status in 15m. tagging support to notify affected customers.
Ben S.: follow-ups created: KMS-342 (backoff fix), KMS-343 (retry policy e2e), KMS-344 (rate-limit smoothing permanent config)
IncidentBot: Incident closed for now? Manual close after all follow-ups assigned.
Ajit K.: closing immediate on-call loop; leaving the incident open for postmortem. good work everyone. :thumbsup:
summary: Automated PagerDuty alert for KMS proxy high 429s due to rotation job requeue/backoff reset; rotation paused, cache fallback enabled, proxy rate smoothing rolled. Handed to overnight oncall. Follow-ups created for backoff fix and permanent rate-limit changes.
